This server goes looking for ads. When a game wants to show you one, it calls here, and this server asks each seller in turn until one has something. Nothing ever answers, so the game waits and gives up.
This server stores the ad itself: the video, the picture, the fake close button. If it does not answer, there is nothing to show you.
While the game loads, this server puts your attention up for auction. Advertisers pay for the seconds that follow. It all happens in a tenth of a second, before you see anything.
It shows you nothing at all. It writes down what you do — which app, when, for how long — and sells it on.
A fake site, put up quickly and abandoned a few weeks later. This is where the ads claiming your phone has a virus come from. This app found it without any list.
Not an ad. This is the software the game is built on, and the game needs it to run. This app lets it through.
Nothing to report. An ordinary server, like the ones behind your messages or your maps.
Tap one to see what it is

One ad = one time a game tried to show you something. To show a single ad, your phone has to contact a dozen servers at once — which is why the list further down is always much longer than this number. AdZero groups them together, so what you see here is ads.
This server has nothing to do with advertising. This app lets it through.
This server exists to deliver ads. This app does not answer it, so the ad never arrives.
This server records what you do, or tries to mislead you. This app blocks it.
Here is what %1$s contacted just before. The likeliest culprit is at the top — block it and that ad will not come back.

During the seconds an ad is loading, silences servers that neither this app nor any other has ever used. This is what catches ads no list knows about.
By default, the one your phone is set to.

Private DNS is in the way
Your phone sends its lookups straight to another server over HTTPS, where AdZero never sees them. Turn Private DNS off in the Android settings, under Network.
Sends the installer alone. WhatsApp, Quick Share, Telegram and Drive all take it; Gmail refuses this kind of attachment.

🚫 Download AdZero — it removes the ads in games, and on the web. Open the attached file to install it. Android will warn that it does not come from the Play Store: that is true and expected, tap install anyway. Nothing to pay, no account to create.\n\n📱 Works in every game. 🎮 No video, no banners. 🔒 Nothing leaves your phone.
Android stops background apps to save power, and on some phones it stops the protection after a few hours without saying so.
Turn the protection on and play for a few minutes. What was blocked, in which game, and how much time you got back will appear here.
Between %1$s and %2$s the ad networks did not get
Where does that figure come from?

An ad pays the app that showed it somewhere between three and twelve dollars per thousand — a rewarded video at the top, a banner at the bottom, and it moves with the country and the season. So this is a range, not a total: the low end assumes every ad you avoided was the cheapest kind. Nobody outside the networks knows the real number, this app included.
Games already open keep the old addresses

A game that looked up an ad server before protection started keeps that address in its own memory for a while, and connects straight to it. Close your open games and reopen them; anything opened from now on is covered.
Close and reopen your games: the ones already running keep the old addresses in memory.
Block the server that just showed you an ad.

Close it and open it again — its ads are already loaded.
Greyed out? Android guards this one for apps installed outside a store. Long-press the AdZero icon → App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then come back.
AdZero silenced %1$d servers for this app. It will release them one at a time, starting with the one this game most likely needs, until it works again.
This one is released. Close the game, open it again and try. Then come back here.
Done. %1$s stays released for every app.
None of them was it, so AdZero is probably not the cause. Everything has been put back.
%1$s ads stream from the same server as the videos themselves. There is no separate address to silence — only one address for both, and blocking it would stop anything from playing.
Sponsored posts in %1$s arrive in the same feed as the real ones, from the company\'s own server. Nothing tells them apart from the outside.

AdZero removes ads that come from servers built only for ads, which is nearly all advertising in games. It cannot remove ads a company serves itself, alongside its own content. No DNS blocker can, and one that claimed otherwise would be lying to you.
Only its trackers are blocked here.

Ads on the sites you open from %1$s are removed like anywhere else. The ones inside the search results themselves are not: those come from the same server as the results, so there is no way to tell them apart.
Press it to protect, press it again to stop. That is the whole app.
